[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

**Adopt GitHub Issues as the primary execution queue for AI autonomous agent tasks**, using structured machine-readable issue templates as the specification format. Azure DevOps remains the system of record for human-governed work items and enterprise traceability.

---
page_texts.6:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell is introducing AI-assisted and AI-autonomous development workflows to accelerate delivery of enterprise architecture artifacts, application components, documentation, and infrastructure. For autonomous agents to function reliably, they require a specification store that acts not just as a record but as an **actionable execution trigger** — one the agent can discover, parse, act upon, and report back to without additional tooling bridges.
page_texts.7:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The enterprise uses two primary work management systems:

- **Azure DevOps** — sprint planning, backlog management, acceptance criteria, test plans, and regulated audit trails
- **GitHub** — source code, CI/CD workflows, Copilot-native AI agents, and GitHub Actions automation

Autonomous AI agents (GitHub Copilot Workspace, custom GitHub Actions agents, and Copilot-assigned issues) are natively integrated into the GitHub platform. Routing agent tasks through ADO introduces authentication complexity, service hook configuration overhead, and a structural mismatch between ADO work item fields and the flat-text context an AI model consumes.
page_texts.8:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a defined execution model, teams will inconsistently store AI-executable specs across ADO, GitHub Issues, repository files, and ad-hoc prompts — preventing repeatable, auditable autonomous workflows and making it impossible to build shared agent pipelines.
page_texts.9:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- 🤖 AI agents (Copilot, GitHub Actions) operate natively on GitHub Issues with no additional auth or field mapping
- 🔁 GitHub Actions webhooks (`issues.opened`, `issues.labeled`) provide zero-configuration event triggers for agent pipelines
- 🏥 HIPAA-adjacent regulated work requires audit trails — ADO remains the system of record for compliance traceability
- ⚡ Reducing the friction between specification and execution shortens the feedback loop for AI-driven delivery
- 📋 Structured markdown templates are machine-readable without custom parsers

---
page_texts.11:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#github-issues-as-ai-agent-execution-queue-with-structured-spec-templates]

### GitHub Issues as AI Agent Execution Queue with Structured Spec Templates

**Description**: GitHub Issues, backed by structured markdown templates enforced via `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, serve as the execution queue for all AI autonomous agent tasks. Issues are the single surface where a spec is written, an agent is triggered, implementation is delivered (via linked PR), and results are reported.

**Phase 1 — Template Standardization**: Define `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` templates with mandatory structured sections (`## Goal`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Constraints`) that agents parse deterministically.

**Phase 2 — Agent Pipeline Wiring**: Implement GitHub Actions workflows that trigger on `issues.labeled` (e.g., `agent-task`) to invoke the appropriate agent, pass the issue body as context, and open a linked pull request with results.

**Phase 3 — ADO Sync for Traceability**: Optionally link GitHub Issues back to ADO work items via `AB#<id>` references in issue bodies, preserving the enterprise audit trail without blocking agent execution.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Zero additional auth — GitHub token is sufficient for agent read/write on issues and PRs
- ✅ Copilot-native: GitHub Copilot can be assigned directly to issues and will open a PR autonomously
- ✅ Event-driven by default — `issues.labeled` triggers fire without polling
- ✅ Markdown-native format — AI models parse issue bodies with no schema translation
- ✅ Full traceability — issue → PR → merge forms a complete audit chain in GitHub
- ✅ Scales to all artifact types (code, docs, IaC, ADRs, patterns) via label-based routing

**Cons**:

- ❌ GitHub Issues lack structured fields (story points, iteration, priority) present in ADO
- ❌ Duplicate data entry required if the spec must also exist in ADO for sprint tracking
- ❌ GitHub is not the primary system of record for regulated compliance artifacts at Gainwell

page_texts.13:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#option-1-azure-devops-work-items-as-spec-store]

### Option 1: Azure DevOps Work Items as Spec Store

**Description**: All AI-executable specs live in ADO work items. GitHub Actions polls ADO or consumes service hook events to retrieve and execute specs.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Single source of truth with enterprise work tracking
- ✅ Rich structured fields (acceptance criteria, iteration, story points, test cases)

**Cons**:

- ❌ Requires separate PAT and org/project routing for agent API access
- ❌ Service hook configuration is non-trivial and brittle across environments
- ❌ ADO work item fields require custom parsing to extract agent context
- ❌ GitHub Copilot native features (issue assignment, Copilot Workspace) do not integrate with ADO
page_texts.14:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#option-2-repository-markdown-files-as-spec-store]

### Option 2: Repository Markdown Files as Spec Store

**Description**: AI-executable specs are checked in as `.md` or `.feature` files in a `specs/` or `tasks/` directory in the repository. Agents are triggered by file creation PRs or file change events.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Version-controlled, diff-able, and always co-located with the code
- ✅ No external system dependency — fully self-contained in the repo
- ✅ Directly readable by any agent without API calls

**Cons**:

- ❌ Requires a PR to create a spec, adding friction before the agent can act
- ❌ No native human collaboration surface (comments, @mentions, reactions)
- ❌ No built-in event model — requires file-change triggers or polling
page_texts.15:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#option-3-hybrid--github-issues-execution--ado-governance]

### Option 3: Hybrid — GitHub Issues (Execution) + ADO (Governance)

**Description**: GitHub Issues serve as the agent execution queue for autonomous tasks. ADO Work Items remain the system of record for sprint planning, backlog governance, and compliance traceability. Issues reference ADO items via `AB#<id>` cross-links.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Each system is used for what it does best
- ✅ Agent execution path is clean and native to GitHub
- ✅ Enterprise audit trail preserved in ADO
- ✅ No forced migration of existing ADO workflows

**Cons**:

- ❌ Dual system maintenance increases authoring overhead
- ❌ Teams must understand and consistently apply the division of responsibility

---
page_texts.16:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option**: **Hybrid — GitHub Issues (Execution) + ADO (Governance)** (Option 3, promoted to Required Option)

**Rationale**: Pure GitHub Issues provides the cleanest agent execution path but abandons Gainwell's existing ADO investment and compliance traceability. Pure ADO creates intractable integration complexity for native AI agents. The hybrid model assigns each system to the job it is architecturally best suited for, while `AB#<id>` cross-links preserve the chain of accountability required in regulated environments.
page_texts.17:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#implementation]

### Implementation

- 🎯 **Key Steps**:
  1. Create `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task.md` with required sections (`Goal`, `Acceptance Criteria`, `Constraints`)
  2. Create `.github/workflows/agent-dispatch.yml` triggered on `issues.labeled` with label `agent-task`
  3. Define label taxonomy: `agent-task`, `agent:implementation`, `agent:documentation`, `agent:testing`, `agent:infrastructure` (see STD-GOV-AI-002)
  4. Document the spec authoring convention — ADO story ID included in issue body via `AB#<id>`
  5. Publish the spec format standard in `standards/governance/`
- 📊 **Success Criteria**: At least one end-to-end autonomous agent cycle (issue → PR → merge) completed with a linked ADO work item within one sprint of adoption

---
page_texts.19:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#-positive]

### ✅ Positive

- AI agents have a clean, zero-friction execution trigger requiring no external system access
- The PR produced by an agent is automatically linked to the originating issue, creating a full audit chain
- Label-based routing allows multiple specialized agents to coexist on the same event bus
- Development teams gain a repeatable, documented pattern for authoring AI-executable specs
- Reduces time from specification to implementation for routine EA artifact generation
page_texts.20:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#-negative]

### ❌ Negative

- Teams must author specs in two places (ADO for sprint tracking, GitHub Issues for agent execution) until an ADO→GitHub sync automation is implemented
- Unstructured or ambiguously written issue bodies will cause agent failures — quality of spec directly determines quality of output
- Governance of agent-produced PRs (who reviews, merge criteria) must be explicitly defined
page_texts.21:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#-neutral]

### ⚪ Neutral

- This model is additive — existing manual GitHub workflows and ADO processes are unchanged
- The structured issue template format is also valid input for human developers, not exclusively for agents

---
page_texts.23:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#-risks]

### ⚠️ Risks

- **Agent Hallucination Risk**: An agent may misinterpret an ambiguously written spec and produce incorrect or incomplete output, which gets merged if review gates are weak
- **Runaway Automation Risk**: A misconfigured label trigger could cause an agent to act on unintended issues, consuming API quota or opening spurious PRs
- **Compliance Gap Risk**: If an agent-produced change is merged without an ADO work item link, the regulated audit trail is broken
- **Privilege Escalation Risk**: Agent workflows operating with broad repository write permissions could be exploited via malicious issue body content (prompt injection)
page_texts.24:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#-mitigations]

### 🛡️ Mitigations

- **Spec Quality Gate**: Require all `agent-task` issues to pass a structural validation action (checks for required sections) before the agent workflow fires
- **Scoped Permissions**: Agent workflows use the minimum required GitHub token scopes (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write` only); never `admin`
- **Mandatory ADO Link Validation**: The agent dispatch workflow validates that the issue body contains an `AB#` reference before invoking the agent; fails with a comment if absent
- **Branch Protection Enforcement**: Agent-produced PRs are subject to the same branch protection rules as human PRs (per ADR-GOV-008) — no auto-merge without a passing review
- **Prompt Injection Hardening**: Agent workflows must sanitize issue body content before passing to model context; never execute issue body as shell commands

---
page_texts.25:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md#compliance-notes]

## Compliance Notes

- **Security**: Agent workflows must follow least-privilege token scoping. Issue body content must be treated as untrusted input — apply prompt injection mitigations before passing to model context. See `strategy/guidance/security/` for Gainwell security routing.
- **Regulatory**: For HIPAA-adjacent work items, the ADO work item remains the official record. GitHub Issues are the execution surface only — they must not contain PHI or PII.
- **Standards**: This decision is consistent with ADR-GOV-008 (source control workflow policies) — agent PRs are subject to all existing branch protection and review requirements.
